title: Evolution and Natural Selection
seo_title: Year 10 Science: Evolution and Natural Selection Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Use the theory of evolution by natural selection to explain past and present diversity and analyse the scientific evidence supporting the theory (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 10 science worksheets on evolution: variation, natural selection, adaptation, selection pressures, speciation, extinction, and evidence from fossils, comparative anatomy and DNA. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Individuals with helpful variations survive, reproduce and pass on their genes.
body_html:
How to think about it

Evolution is a change in the inherited traits of a population over many generations.

  • Natural selection: variation exists; a selection pressure acts; the best suited survive and reproduce; their alleles become more common.
  • Isolated populations can change so much they form new species (speciation).
  • Evidence: fossils in rock layers, homologous structures, embryos and DNA similarities.
Example

Myxomatosis 1950: why more resistant rabbits later?

some rabbits had resistance

they survived and bred

Answer: resistance alleles became common

Example

Human arm and whale flipper: same bones. Evidence of?

homologous structures

Answer: a common ancestor

Common mistakes

  • Thinking an individual changes during its life to survive.
  • Thinking organisms change because they 'need' or 'want' to.
  • Thinking evolution has a goal or always makes organisms 'better'.

faq.q: What is the difference between natural selection and evolution?
faq.a: Natural selection is the process: individuals with useful traits survive and reproduce more. Evolution is the result: the population's traits change over generations.

faq.q: Why are antibiotic-resistant bacteria a problem?
faq.a: When antibiotics are overused, resistant bacteria survive and multiply, so infections become harder to treat.
Fossils in rock layers, similar bone structures in different species, similar early embryos, and DNA sequences that are more alike in closely related species.

items.q: Some Tasmanian devils now show resistance to devil facial tumour disease. What explains this?
c: Devils with resistance genes survived and passed them on.
Devils learned to avoid the tumour.
The disease went away by itself.
items.e: Selection is changing the population.

items.q: A weightlifter builds big muscles. Will her children inherit them?
c: No. Acquired traits are not inherited.
items.e: Only genes are inherited.

items.q: What is an adaptation?
c: an inherited trait that helps an organism survive and reproduce in its environment
a change an animal makes during its life
items.e: Shaped by selection.

items.q: Is whether ear lobes are attached or free an example of continuous or discontinuous variation?
items.e: Continuous: any value in a range (column graph with no gaps, or histogram). Discontinuous: distinct groups.

items.q: Some beetles in a population are green and some are brown, and colour is passed to offspring. Which factor of natural selection does this show?
c: better-adapted individuals survive and reproduce more
items.e: The four factors: overproduction, variation, competition and differential survival.

items.q: Is natural hair colour caused by genes, by the environment, or by both?
items.e: Some features are inherited, some come from how we live, and many depend on both.

items.q: Does natural selection act on individuals or populations?
c: It acts on individuals, but populations evolve.
items.e: Allele frequencies change.

items.q: Some Australian snakes now have smaller heads in areas with cane toads. Why?
c: Snakes with small heads cannot swallow big toxic toads, so they survive and breed.
Small heads are a mutation in every snake.
Snakes shrank their heads on purpose.
items.e: This is natural selection in action.

items.q: A mutation gives a few bacteria a gene that breaks down an antibiotic. Which factor of natural selection does this show?
c: better-adapted individuals survive and reproduce more
items.e: The four factors: overproduction, variation, competition and differential survival.

items.q: A cod lays millions of eggs, but only a few grow up. Which factor of natural selection does this show?
c: better-adapted individuals survive and reproduce more
items.e: The four factors: overproduction, variation, competition and differential survival.

items.q: Is blood group caused by genes, by the environment, or by both?
items.e: Some features are inherited, some come from how we live, and many depend on both.

items.q: Is hand span an example of continuous or discontinuous variation?
items.e: Continuous: any value in a range (column graph with no gaps, or histogram). Discontinuous: distinct groups.

items.q: Is blood group an example of continuous or discontinuous variation?
items.e: Continuous: any value in a range (column graph with no gaps, or histogram). Discontinuous: distinct groups.

items.q: What are homologous structures?
c: similar structures in different species that come from a common ancestor
structures with the same use but different origins
items.e: The forelimbs of humans, whales and bats.

items.q: Is a scar from a fall caused by genes, by the environment, or by both?
items.e: Some features are inherited, some come from how we live, and many depend on both.

items.q: Only a few nesting sites are on a small island, and many birds want them. Which factor of natural selection does this show?
c: better-adapted individuals survive and reproduce more
items.e: The four factors: overproduction, variation, competition and differential survival.

items.q: Who proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection?
c: Charles Darwin and Alfred Russel Wallace
items.e: Darwin visited Australia on HMS Beagle in 1836.

items.q: Why do many marsupials live only in Australia?
c: Australia was isolated for millions of years, so marsupials evolved into many forms here.
items.e: Isolation led to adaptive radiation.

items.q: Is whether you can roll your tongue an example of continuous or discontinuous variation?
items.e: Continuous: any value in a range (column graph with no gaps, or histogram). Discontinuous: distinct groups.

items.q: Moths that match the tree bark are eaten less and leave more offspring. Which factor of natural selection does this show?
c: better-adapted individuals survive and reproduce more
items.e: The four factors: overproduction, variation, competition and differential survival.

items.q: 20 000 bacteria are in a culture, and 10% are resistant. An antibiotic kills every non-resistant cell. How many are killed (Ethan's lab)?
After a drought on a Galápagos island, only large, hard seeds were left. The next generation of finches had deeper beaks. Which explanation is best?
c: The environment does not affect which individuals survive.
Finches with deeper beaks survived to breed.
All individuals changed in the same way during their lives.
Each finch's beak grew to fit the seeds.
items.e: Natural selection acts on traits that are already present and inherited.

items.q: Priya's sample has 20 000 bacteria. 5% of them have a resistance gene. An antibiotic kills all the others. How many bacteria are left?
Some HIV viruses in a patient change their surface proteins and escape a drug. Which explanation is best?
c: All individuals changed in the same way during their lives.
The environment does not affect which individuals survive.
Variants the drug cannot stop survive and multiply.
items.e: Natural selection acts on traits that are already present and inherited.

items.q: Hunters target the largest elk antlers, and average antler size shrinks. Which type of selection is this?
items.e: One extreme is favored, so the average shifts.

items.q: Why does an individual organism not evolve?
c: Evolution is a change in the gene pool of a population over generations.
items.e: Populations evolve; individuals do not.

items.q: Cane toads spread across Australia. Toads at the front of the spread now have longer legs. A student says: “Toads stretched their legs by hopping, and their young inherited it.” What is wrong with this claim?
c: Evolution is too slow to see.
Individuals do not change their genes to meet a need; selection acts on existing variation.
items.e: That is Lamarck's idea, not natural selection.

items.q: In a lake, small-beaked and large-beaked birds survive, but medium beaks cannot handle either seed type. Which type of selection is this?
items.e: Both extremes are favored, so the population splits.

items.q: What is a selection pressure?
c: a factor in the environment that affects which individuals survive and reproduce
a force that changes DNA on purpose
items.e: Predators, disease and climate are examples.

items.q: After an antibiotic, the 10 survivors in Mei's culture are all resistant and multiply. What percent of the new population is resistant?
items.e: Only resistant cells were left to reproduce.

items.q: Ethan studies beach mice on white sand dunes where owls hunt by sight. Why do individuals with light-coloured fur leave more offspring?
c: Their trait helps them survive long enough to reproduce and pass it on.
They decided to change their trait.
Their trait appeared because they needed it.
items.e: Natural selection acts on traits that already vary.

items.q: Zara studies a population of rock pocket mice with dark fur or light fur on black lava rock where hawks hunt. Which individuals are most likely to survive and reproduce?
items.e: The trait that helps in this environment is dark fur.

items.q: Clutch size in a bird: too few eggs means few chicks, too many means chicks starve, so medium clutches do best. Which type of selection is this?
items.e: The middle is favored, so variation shrinks.

items.q: A doctor's patient stops taking antibiotics early. The infection comes back and the drug no longer works. Which explanation is best?
c: All individuals changed in the same way during their lives.
The bacteria learned to resist the drug.
The environment does not affect which individuals survive.
items.e: Natural selection acts on traits that are already present and inherited.

items.q: Fish with medium body size survive best in a stream with both fast current and predators. Which type of selection is this?
items.e: The middle is favored, so variation shrinks.

items.q: Cane toads spread across Australia. Toads at the front of the spread now have longer legs. Which explanation is best?
c: The environment does not affect which individuals survive.
Toads stretched their legs by hopping, and their young inherited it.
Toads with longer legs reached new areas first and bred there.
All individuals changed in the same way during their lives.
items.e: Natural selection acts on traits that are already present and inherited.

items.q: Priya predicts how fish in a stream with many predators will change over many generations. What is most likely?
c: The percent with duller colours will increase.
The traits will stay exactly the same.
The percent with bright colours will increase.
Every individual will change its trait during its life.
items.e: Helpful heritable traits become more common.

items.q: A farmer sprays the same insecticide for years. It kills fewer insects each year. Which explanation is best?
c: Insects with resistance genes survived and passed them on.
All individuals changed in the same way during their lives.
Each insect got used to the spray.
The environment does not affect which individuals survive.
items.e: Natural selection acts on traits that are already present and inherited.

items.q: Noah studies a population of bacteria with resistance to an antibiotic or no resistance in a patient taking that antibiotic. Which individuals are most likely to survive and reproduce?
c: those with resistance to an antibiotic
items.e: The trait that helps in this environment is resistance to an antibiotic.

items.q: Amelia's sample has 20 000 bacteria. 1% of them have a resistance gene. An antibiotic kills all the others. How many bacteria are left?
A fungus disease spread and wiped out several frog species. Which result of environmental change is this?
items.e: Change can help some species, make new ones and end others.

items.q: Why does biodiversity matter?
c: Ecosystems with many species are more stable and give us food, medicines and materials.
items.e: Species change over long periods; some die out.

items.q: What are the main steps of natural selection?
c: individuals change on purpose to survive
variation, selection pressure, survival and reproduction of the best suited, inheritance
items.e: Darwin and Wallace described this in 1858.

items.q: Two snail species have shells that coil in opposite directions, so their bodies cannot line up to mate. Which kind of isolation is this?
items.e: Body parts do not fit.

items.q: Why do scientists compare DNA sequences between species?
c: DNA shows the age of rocks.
Closely related species have more similar DNA.
DNA is the same in all species.
items.e: DNA evidence supports common ancestry.

items.q: Which of these can cause extinction?
c: loss of habitat, new diseases, new predators and climate change
items.e: Species change over long periods; some die out.

items.q: Ethan graphed rabbits in a snowy forest with foxes (x-axis: generation). What does the graph show?
c: White winter fur became less common over time.
Each animal changed its trait during its life.
White winter fur became more common over time.
items.e: The bars rise across generations.

items.q: Using Lachlan's graph, by how many percentage points did light-coloured fur rise from generation 1 to generation 10?
An asteroid impact ended the age of dinosaurs. Which result of environmental change is this?
items.e: Change can help some species, make new ones and end others.

items.q: A lake dries up, and deer have more grassland to graze. Why did one species increase?
c: Every species increases after any change.
The change gave it more resources or removed a limit on its numbers.
It chose to have more young.
items.e: Changes help some species and harm others.

items.q: Two pine species release pollen in different months. Which kind of isolation is this?
items.e: Different breeding times.

items.q: What is a species?
c: a group of organisms that can breed to produce fertile offspring
all the animals in a habitat
items.e: Species change over long periods; some die out.

items.q: The golden toad of Costa Rica disappeared after its cloud forest became warmer and drier. Why did the species go extinct?
c: It became a new species overnight.
It could not survive or adapt fast enough to the change.
items.e: Change was faster than adaptation.

items.q: A few finches are blown to a distant island and never return. Which kind of isolation is this?
items.e: A physical barrier separates them.

items.q: Why is a mule (horse × donkey) not a separate species?
c: Mules are infertile and cannot breed.
items.e: Species change over long periods; some die out.

items.q: Using Zara's graph, by how many percentage points did dark wings rise from generation 1 to generation 10?
What is speciation?
c: the formation of a new species, often after populations are separated
items.e: Isolated populations change in different ways.

items.q: Two flower species have shapes that fit different pollinators. Which kind of isolation is this?
items.e: Body parts do not fit.

items.q: Apple maggot flies began laying eggs on apples instead of hawthorn and are becoming separate species. Which result of environmental change is this?
items.e: Change can help some species, make new ones and end others.

items.q: A new highway and city cut a forest in two, and salamanders cannot cross. Which kind of isolation is this?
items.e: A physical barrier separates them.

c: an earlier species that two or more living species evolved from
a species alive today that others came from

items.q: Rabbits in Australia were infected with the myxoma virus in 1950. Within years, more rabbits survived it. Why?
c: Every rabbit became resistant during its life.
Rabbits with natural resistance survived and passed it on to their offspring.
Rabbits learned to avoid the virus.
The virus made rabbits stronger on purpose.

items.q: What are homologous structures?
c: parts that do the same job in unrelated species
body parts with similar bones because of a shared ancestor
items.e: Arm, flipper, wing.

items.q: What kind of structures are these: a shark fin and a dolphin flipper?
items.e: Same job, different build: no close common ancestor.

items.q: Kai compares skulls of different finches with different beaks. What type of evidence is this?
items.e: Beak shape matches the food they eat.

items.q: DNA, fossils and anatomy all show birds are close to crocodiles. Why does this agreement matter?
c: It proves the fossils are wrong.
Independent evidence supports the same claim.
It shows the data are copied.
items.e: Multiple lines of evidence.

items.q: A student says whales are fish because they swim. Which evidence shows whales are mammals?
c: whale flipper bones and DNA match mammals
items.e: Homologous bones and DNA.

items.q: Why do doctors tell patients to finish all their antibiotics?
c: to kill the bacteria before resistant ones can multiply
items.e: Prevents selection for resistance.

items.q: A trait that helps in one environment harms in another. What does this show?
items.e: No perfect organism.

items.q: Ruby graphs the percentage of resistant rabbits from 1950 to 1960. It rises from 5% to 60%. What does this show?
c: the resistant trait became more common through natural selection
items.e: Change in a population over generations.

items.q: Mia models natural selection with coloured paper 'moths' on a newspaper background. Which colour will 'survive' best?
c: grey moths that match the newspaper
items.e: Camouflage reduces predation.

items.q: Which finding would best support a common ancestor of two species?
c: many shared DNA sequences and homologous bones
items.e: Shared inherited traits.

items.q: Why can't natural selection make a trait that is not in the population?
c: It can make any trait it needs.
Selection only acts on variation that already exists.
items.e: Mutation supplies new variation.

Why does evolution happen faster in bacteria than in elephants?
c: Bacteria reproduce much faster, so there are many generations quickly.
items.e: Generation time.
